category: Capture menus, utilities, PCB-flow properties and Capture file types
description: OrCAD Capture commands and utilities not covered by the core editing catalog (Generate Part, Split Part, Library Correction, Push Occurrence Properties, Assign Power Pins, Create Differential Pair, Intersheet References, Auto Wire, NetGroups, locking, label states, macros, test benches, placement report), the Part Editor's pin and package commands, the Preferences dialog and Capture.ini, the properties and configuration that drive the Capture-to-PCB Editor flow (ROOM, SWAP_INFO, NO_SWAP_*, allegro.cfg, pst*.dat), and the Capture file types (.dsn, .opj, .olb, .drc, .bom, .xrf, .exp, .upd, .swp, .mnl, .dbk/.obk). Menu paths follow the Capture 16.6-17.4 user guide; OrCAD X Capture keeps most of them.

tools.name: Tools > Generate Part
tools.description: Creates a library part automatically from a source such as a PSpice model library, a netlist or the hierarchical ports of the root schematic (for design reuse). If the destination .olb does not exist Capture creates it, and for design-based parts the new part references the source schematic so descending the hierarchy opens it.
tools.usage: Tools > Generate Part > Netlist/source file, Netlist/source file type, Part name, Destination part library, options > OK

parameters.name: Netlist/source file type
parameters.description: e.g. PSpice Model Library, Capture schematic/design, and other supported sources.

tools.example: Tools > Generate Part > source = vendor_opamps.lib (PSpice Model Library) > part name OPA_X > destination mylib.olb: a symbol with PSPICETEMPLATE and IMPLEMENTATION already set.
tools.notes: To create a pin with Generate Part the pin must have a pin-to-port mapping in the pin file. Review pin placement afterwards in the Part Editor.

tools.name: Tools > Split Part
tools.description: Splits a single-section library part (for example a large FPGA or BGA) into several sections using the Split Part Section Input Spreadsheet, assigning pins to sections and choosing numeric or alphabetic section suffixes. The result is a heterogeneous multi-section part that is easier to spread across pages.
tools.usage: Select the part in the library folder of the Project Manager > Tools > Split Part (or right-click > Split Part)

parameters.name: Part Numbering
parameters.description: Numeric (1-1024) or Alphabetic (A-Z) suffix per section.

parameters.name: Section input spreadsheet
parameters.description: Pin-to-section assignment; add or delete pins.

tools.example: Split XC7A35T_CSG324 into banks: section per I/O bank plus power and configuration sections.
tools.notes: Only single-section parts, or parts previously split with this spreadsheet, can be split.

tools.name: Accessories > LibCorrectionUtil (Library Correction Utility)
tools.description: Verifies or corrects part libraries before the Capture-PCB Editor flow: fills missing pin numbers from pin names, finds duplicate pin names, changes pin name/number casing and makes power pins visible. It writes a log such as <Library_name>Miss.log next to the library.
tools.usage: Accessories > LibCorrectionUtil > Library Verification/Correction > Select Library for Correction > options > Verify or Correct

parameters.name: Missing Pin Numbers
parameters.description: Copies pin names into empty pin numbers.

parameters.name: Duplicate Pin Names / Casing / Power Pins Visible

tools.example: Run Verify on legacy.olb, read legacyMiss.log, then Correct and re-save the library.
tools.notes: Back up the library first. The Tcl utility capLibUtil::checkPkgs / correctPkgs in the Tcl app note performs similar package checks from a script.

tools.name: Accessories > Push Occ. Prop into Instance
tools.description: Converts an occurrence-mode design to instance mode: transfers occurrence values of part reference and PCB footprint to instance properties, moves flat-net occurrence values to schematic nets, and optionally removes all occurrence properties and sets the design's preferred mode to instance.
tools.usage: Accessories > Push Occ. Prop into Instance > Transfer Occ. Prop. to Instance

parameters.name: Remove occurrence level properties
parameters.description: Deletes occurrence properties after transfer and switches to instance mode.

tools.example: Before reusing a single-instance hierarchical block elsewhere, push its occurrence references and footprints into instances.
tools.notes: Not appropriate for designs that genuinely need different values per occurrence (complex hierarchy reused several times).

tools.name: Tools > Assign Power Pins
tools.description: Shows the invisible power pins of a selected component or of the whole design with the power net each connects to, and lets you reassign them to other power nets. The choice is stored in the POWER_GROUP property of the component, avoiding pin-by-pin edits.
tools.usage: Select a part instance or the root design > Tools > Assign Power Pins > Power Names column drop-down > OK
tools.example: Reassign VCC of U12 (a 3.3 V logic part) from VCC to +3V3, save, and check POWER_GROUP in the Property Editor.
tools.notes: Related properties: POWER_PINS on parts and PSPICEDEFAULTNET for simulation. Invisible power pins are a common cause of unexpected net merges in the PCB netlist.

tools.name: Tools > Create Differential Pair
tools.description: Creates, modifies or deletes differential pairs between flat nets from Capture (an alternative to typing the DIFFERENTIAL_PAIR net property), including creating many pairs at once from name patterns. The pairs flow into PCB Editor and Constraint Manager with the netlist.
tools.usage: Select the .dsn or a page > Tools > Create Differential Pair > Filter, All Nets, Selections > Create

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: Show nets starting with typed letters.

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: The two nets forming the pair.

tools.example: Filter USB_ > select USB_DP and USB_DN > name USB_D > Create.

tools.name: Tools > Intersheet References
tools.description: Adds (or removes) page references next to off-page connectors and hierarchical ports showing where the same signal appears; in hierarchical designs a trailing ! means one level lower and ^ one level higher. A report of the references can also be generated.
tools.usage: Tools > Intersheet References > Place/Delete, options for flat or hierarchical designs and report
tools.example: In a flat 12-page design, Tools > Intersheet References so every off-page connector shows e.g. '3,7' for the pages carrying that net.

tools.name: Place > Auto Wire (Two Points, Multiple Points, Connect to Bus)
tools.description: Routes schematic wires automatically between picked points: pin-to-pin, pin-to-wire or wire-to-wire for two points, a whole set of picked points, or connects selected pins/wires to a bus (and, in newer releases, to NetGroups) with generated member names.
tools.usage: Place > Auto Wire > Two Points | Multiple Points | Connect to Bus
tools.example: Place > Auto Wire > Connect to Bus, select the eight data pins of U3, click the bus DATA[0..7] and accept the proposed net names.

tools.name: Place > NetGroup
tools.description: Creates and places NetGroups, named or unnamed collections of scalars, buses and nested NetGroups that travel as one connection across pages and hierarchy (for interfaces such as DDR or PCIe). Named definitions can be exported and imported as XML and reused as blocks, hierarchical ports or off-page connectors.
tools.usage: Place > NetGroup > Place / Create NetGroup dialog: Add NetGroup, Add member (NetGroup, bus with width, scalar)

parameters.name: Member width
parameters.description: Buses and nested groups need a range, e.g. AD[0..4].

tools.example: Create NetGroup SPI with scalars SCLK, MOSI, MISO, CS_N and place it as a hierarchical port on the sensor block.
tools.notes: Introduced in the 16.6 generation; older netlisters and downstream tools may need the flattened member nets.

tools.name: Edit > Lock / Unlock (graphical operation locking)
tools.description: Locks objects on a page, pages in a folder, folders in a design, or the whole design against graphical changes (move, delete, edit), with cascading and roll-up behaviour; locked Project Manager objects show a lock icon. The lock state must be saved with the design.
tools.usage: Select object(s) > Edit > Lock (or right-click > Lock); Edit > Unlock
tools.example: Lock the reviewed power-supply page before others edit the rest of the design.
tools.notes: Project Manager objects must be locked one at a time; schematic objects can be multi-selected.

tools.name: Edit > Label State (Set, Goto, Delete)
tools.description: Defines named checkpoints of a schematic page so you can try what-if edits and return to the saved state. Each page has implicit Start and End states; user labels are one to five alphanumeric characters and are case-insensitive.
tools.usage: Edit > Label State > Set <label> | Goto <label> | Delete <label>
tools.example: Edit > Label State > Set ALT1, rework the filter topology, and Edit > Label State > Goto ALT1 if the change is rejected.
tools.notes: Labels cannot be named Start or End.

tools.name: Macro > Record / Play / Configure (Capture macros)
tools.description: Records schematic-editor actions as a macro, with buttons to stop, pause, or record a command 'with dialog' so it prompts for a value on playback. Temporary macros can be saved and named in Configure, given shortcut keys, and played back; macro commands such as PlacePart, PlaceWire and FindParts are documented in the Macro Command Reference.
tools.usage: Click a start location > Macro > Record; Macro > Configure (Save, Add, Remove, shortcut); Macro > Play
tools.example: Record placing a decoupling capacitor with its GND symbol, save it as DECAP, bind it to a key and replay at each IC.
tools.notes: Macro command names are reserved words. The Tcl command window is the more powerful successor for new automation.

tools.name: Tools > Test Bench > Create Test Bench (partial design simulation)
tools.description: Creates a test bench under TestBenches in the Project Manager that contains the master design with all components greyed out; you activate only the parts you want to simulate and add stimuli, then compare and update changes back to the master design.
tools.usage: Select the .dsn > Tools > Test Bench > Create Test Bench > name > OK; right-click the test bench > Make Active
tools.example: Create TB_FILTER, activate only the anti-alias filter components, add a VAC source and simulate that section alone.

tools.name: Reports > Export Placement (Placements.csv)
tools.description: Generates a CSV report of part placements on the schematic: reference designator, part name, schematic, sheet number, library location and X/Y coordinates, for a design, folder, page or multi-selection. The file is written next to the design and opened for viewing.
tools.usage: Select a level in the Project Manager > right-click > Reports > Export Placement
tools.example: Export Placement for the whole design and use the page/X/Y columns to script cross-probing annotations.

tools.name: Options > Preferences
tools.description: Application-wide Capture preferences on several tabs: Colors/Print (object colours and print inclusion), Grid Display (style, spacing, snap), Pan and Zoom (zoom factor, auto-scroll), Select (area select mode, high-resolution drag limit, tool palette), Miscellaneous (fill, line and colour defaults, Project Manager/Session Log font, intertool communication, text rendering, Auto Recovery interval) and Text Editor.
tools.usage: Options > Preferences > Colors/Print | Grid Display | Pan and Zoom | Select | Miscellaneous | Text Editor

parameters.name: Enable inter-tool communication
parameters.description: Required for cross-probing with PSpice and PCB Editor.

tools.example: Options > Preferences > Miscellaneous > Enable inter-tool communication, when PCB Editor highlights do not reach Capture.
tools.notes: Stored in Capture.ini. Design-specific defaults (fonts, title block, page size, grid reference, hierarchy) are in Options > Design Template instead.

tools.name: Capture.ini
tools.description: Capture's initialisation file storing preferences, library and CIS settings, toolbars, test bench defaults and other options. By default it is created in %HOME%/cdssetup/OrCAD_Capture/<release>, copied from the installation's INI if one exists; Capture can be re-initialised by renaming it.
tools.usage: %HOME%\cdssetup\OrCAD_Capture\<release>\Capture.ini (Tcl: GetIniPath)
tools.example:
[TEST BENCH]
Default Test Bench Name=MyTestBench
tools.notes: Close Capture before editing. A corrupt Capture.ini is a frequent cause of odd GUI behaviour; rename it to force defaults.

tools.name: Auto Recovery and FILES.ASL
tools.description: Capture periodically saves modified open designs and libraries (every 5-120 minutes, set in Preferences > Miscellaneous) to the Windows TEMP directory and keeps FILES.ASL listing the files that were open, so work can be recovered after a crash. Recovered copies are removed on normal exit.
tools.usage: Options > Preferences > Miscellaneous > Auto Recovery interval; recovery file list: <TEMP>\FILES.ASL
tools.example: Set Auto Recovery to 10 minutes on long schematic sessions.
tools.notes: Auto recovery is not an auto-save: if you exit without saving intentionally, changes are lost.

tools.name: Place > Pin / Pin Array (Part Editor)
tools.description: Adds single pins or a row/column of pins to a part in the Part view of the part editor. Pin Array auto-increments names and numbers ending in digits by a positive or negative increment, which speeds up connector and IC symbol creation.
tools.usage: Part Editor: Place > Pin | Place > Pin Array (Starting name, Starting number, Number of pins, Increment, Pin spacing, Shape, Type)

parameters.name: Starting name / number
parameters.description: Up to 128 characters; trailing numbers increment.

tools.example: Place > Pin Array: name D0, number 2, 8 pins, increment 1 -> D0..D7 on pins 2..9.

tools.name: Place > IEEE Symbol (Part Editor)
tools.description: Places IEEE/IEC logic qualifying symbols (Schmitt trigger, open collector, tristate, clock and similar) inside a part body. They are purely graphical and do not affect netlists.
tools.usage: Part Editor: Place > IEEE Symbol > choose from Symbols list > place
tools.example: Add the Schmitt-trigger symbol to the body of a 74HC14 gate.

tools.name: View > Package / View > Convert (Part Editor)
tools.description: Part editor view switches: View > Package shows all sections of a multi-part package (and its pin package properties), View > Convert switches to the alternate (De Morgan/convert) body of the current section.
tools.usage: Part Editor: View > Package | View > Part; View > Convert | View > Normal
tools.example: Open a 74LS00, View > Package to check all four gates share pins 7 and 14, then View > Convert to draw the OR-with-inverted-inputs body.

tools.name: Package Properties spreadsheet (Part Editor, Package view)
tools.description: Spreadsheet listing every pin of the package with its package properties (numbers, names, pin groups, ignore flags and similar). Unlike the Browse spreadsheet it cannot add or remove properties, but has Update and Validate buttons to push and check edits.
tools.usage: Part Editor in Package view > Edit > Properties (or Options > Package Properties for package-level settings)
tools.example: Set PIN_GROUP values for swappable resistor-network pins, Validate, then Update.

tools.name: Design > New Part / New Symbol (library)
tools.description: With a library selected in the Project Manager, New Part opens the New Part Properties dialog (name, prefix, PCB footprint, parts per package, homogeneous/heterogeneous, alphabetic/numeric numbering) and the part editor; New Symbol creates power, ground, off-page, port or title block symbols.
tools.usage: Select the .olb in the Project Manager > Design > New Part | New Symbol

parameters.name: Parts per Pkg / Package Type
parameters.description: Number of sections, homogeneous or heterogeneous.

parameters.name: PCB Footprint
parameters.description: Default footprint name for the PCB flow.

tools.example: Design > New Part: LM358, prefix U, footprint SOIC8, 2 parts per package, homogeneous.

tools.name: PSpice > Simulate Selected Profile(s)
tools.description: Simulates several selected simulation profiles in one go: PSpice opens and processes them through its simulation queue. Results are then opened as .DAT files and displayed with Display Control.
tools.usage: Select profiles in the Project Manager (Ctrl+click) > PSpice > Simulate Selected Profile(s)
tools.example: Select TRAN, AC and NOISE profiles > Simulate Selected Profile(s) > afterwards File > Open the three .DAT files in PSpice.

tools.name: Combined property strings ({Property}{Property})
tools.description: A combined property string is one or more property names in braces, optionally mixed with literal text, that Capture expands to property values. Annotate, Bill of Materials, Create Netlist, Update Properties and Cross Reference use them to group, match or format parts.
tools.usage: {Value}{PCB Footprint}  |  {Item}\t{Quantity}\t{Reference}\t{Value}
tools.example: BOM header 'Item\tQuantity\tReference\tPart\tFootprint' with combined property '{Item}\t{Quantity}\t{Reference}\t{Value}\t{PCB Footprint}'.
tools.notes: The Annotate 'Combined property string' decides which parts may share a package: parts with different values or POWER_GROUP must not be combined.

tools.name: ROOM (component property)
tools.description: Instance property grouping components for placement: components with the same ROOM value are placed into the matching room defined in PCB Editor (by Quickplace or placement by room). Set it in the Property Editor in Capture so the grouping is carried by the netlist.
tools.usage: Property Editor: ROOM = <room name>
tools.example: ROOM=PSU on all power-supply parts; in PCB Editor draw a room outline named PSU and place by room.

tools.name: SWAP_INFO / SPLIT_INST (pin swapping properties)
tools.description: Properties enabling pin swaps between sections of heterogeneous (split) packages in the Capture-PCB Editor flow. SWAP_INFO lists logical sections that may exchange pins, e.g. (S1+S2),(S3+S4+S5),(S6+S7), with pins swappable when their PIN_GROUP values match; SPLIT_INST is the alternative for split instances. SWAP_INFO must be enabled in allegro.cfg.
tools.usage: Part property SWAP_INFO = (S1+S2),(S3+S4); allegro.cfg: [ComponentDefinitionProps] SWAP_INFO=YES
tools.example: FPGA split into banks: SWAP_INFO=(S1+S2+S3+S4) on every section so PCB Editor can swap I/O pins between banks with the same PIN_GROUP.
tools.notes: Do not replace the old SPLIT property with SWAP_INFO in existing designs: SPLIT makes parts flat while SWAP_INFO keeps them split, which rips components up on the board.

tools.name: NO_SWAP_COMP / NO_SWAP_GATE / NO_SWAP_GATE_EXT / NO_SWAP_PIN (swap-prevention properties)
tools.description: Properties that forbid specific kinds of swapping in PCB Editor for a component: swapping the whole component, gates within the package, gates to external packages, or pins. They protect functionally critical sections while allowing swaps elsewhere.
tools.usage: Property Editor: NO_SWAP_PIN = TRUE (and similarly for the others)
tools.example: NO_SWAP_GATE=TRUE on a comparator whose sections have different threshold networks.

tools.name: allegro.cfg (Capture PCB Editor netlist configuration)
tools.description: Configuration file of Capture's PCB Editor (Allegro) netlister that decides which Capture properties are passed to the board, in sections such as [ComponentDefinitionProps], [ComponentInstanceProps] and net property sections, and allows aliasing property names. User-defined properties only reach PCB Editor if listed here.
tools.usage: Tools > Create Netlist > PCB Editor tab > Setup > Configuration file (allegro.cfg)
tools.example:
[ComponentDefinitionProps]
SWAP_INFO=YES
; add user-defined properties you want on the board in the matching section, e.g.
[ComponentInstanceProps]
ASSEMBLY_NOTE=YES
tools.notes: Keep a project copy rather than editing the installation copy, and follow the Capture user guide's guidelines for updating allegro.cfg; section names and default entries vary slightly between releases, so start from the copy shipped with your version.

tools.name: pstchip.dat / pstxnet.dat / pstxprt.dat (third-party netlist files)
tools.description: The three files of the Cadence 'Allegro' netlist written by Capture's PCB Editor netlist: pstchip.dat holds part (chip) definitions and pin data, pstxnet.dat the nets and connected pins, pstxprt.dat the part instances and their properties. PCB Editor reads them with File > Import > Logic (netrev).
tools.usage: Tools > Create Netlist > PCB Editor tab > Netlist Files directory (typically <project>\allegro)
tools.example: D:\proj\amp\allegro\pstchip.dat, pstxnet.dat, pstxprt.dat -> PCB Editor: File > Import > Logic > Cadence > Import directory = ..\allegro
tools.notes: Import errors are listed in netrev.lst in the board directory; missing footprints or duplicate pin numbers in pstchip.dat are the usual causes.

tools.name: .dsn
tools.description: OrCAD Capture design file: a binary database with all schematic folders, pages, part instances, nets, properties and the design cache of one design. It is referenced by the .opj project and is the input to netlisting, PSpice and CIS.
tools.usage: File > Open > Design (*.dsn); referenced from <project>.opj
tools.example: D:\proj\amp\amp.dsn
tools.notes: Saving creates a .DBK backup. Designs saved in a newer release cannot be opened by older ones; use File > Save As an older version where offered.

tools.name: .opj
tools.description: OrCAD Capture project file that references the design, libraries, outputs, PSpice resources and other files belonging to the project. It is a small text file; the design data lives in the .dsn.
tools.usage: File > Open > Project (*.opj)
tools.example: Open amp.opj to get the Project Manager with Design Resources, Outputs and PSpice Resources folders.

tools.name: .olb
tools.description: Capture part library file holding parts, symbols (power, ground, off-page, title blocks) and optionally schematic pages; saving it creates an .OBK backup. Libraries must be added to the project or the Place Part library list to be used.
tools.usage: File > New > Library; File > Open > Library; Place > Part > Add Library
tools.example: C:\Cadence\SPB_17.4\tools\capture\library\discrete.olb

tools.name: .drc (Design Rules Check report)
tools.description: Text report written by Tools > Design Rules Check listing electrical and physical rule violations with their locations; the same violations appear as DRC markers on the pages.
tools.usage: Tools > Design Rules Check > Report File: <design>.drc
tools.example: amp.drc listing floating pins, unconnected nets and duplicate references.

tools.name: .bom and .inc (Bill of Materials report and include file)
tools.description: .BOM is the bill-of-materials report produced by Tools > Bill of Materials; an .INC include file can merge extra per-part information (for example part numbers) into the BOM by matching combined property strings.
tools.usage: Tools > Bill of Materials > Report File <design>.BOM; Include File <file>.INC
tools.example: amp.bom with 'Item Quantity Reference Part Footprint' columns, extended through parts.inc with manufacturer part numbers.

tools.name: .xrf (cross reference report)
tools.description: Cross reference report written by Tools > Cross Reference, listing parts by schematic page with part reference, part name and library, optionally with unused sections of multi-part packages and part coordinates.
tools.usage: Tools > Cross Reference > Report File <design>.XRF
tools.example: amp.xrf used by assembly staff to find which page shows U12B.
tools.notes: Capture chooses instances or occurrences automatically: instances for FPGA and PSpice projects, occurrences for PCB and schematic projects.

tools.name: .exp (export properties file)
tools.description: Tab-delimited text file produced by Tools > Export Properties containing part, net or pin properties for editing in a spreadsheet; edited files are read back with Tools > Import Properties.
tools.usage: Tools > Export Properties > <design>.EXP; Tools > Import Properties
tools.example: Export part properties, fill the PCB Footprint column in Excel, save as tab-delimited text, then Import Properties.
tools.notes: Keep the header lines and object identifiers intact, or the import cannot match objects.

tools.name: .upd (update properties file)
tools.description: ASCII file used by Tools > Update Properties. The first line is a header whose first combined property string names the properties to match; the remaining header strings name the properties to set. Each following line gives a match value and the new values. Strings are quoted, at most 124 characters, and text after a semicolon is a comment; results go to an .RPT report.
tools.usage:
"{Net Name}" "Track Width" "Net Spacing"
"VCC" "30" "12"   ; comment
tools.example:
"{Value}" "PCB Footprint"
"10k" "R0603"
"100n" "C0402"

tools.name: .swp (swap file: CHANGEREF, GATESWAP, PINSWAP, CHANGEPIN)
tools.description: Back-annotation input used by Tools > Back Annotate. Each line performs one action: CHANGEREF renames a reference (the default when no keyword is given), GATESWAP swaps parts or gates, PINSWAP swaps two pins of the same type and shape on one part and may be repeated, CHANGEPIN changes one pin to another and may be used once per pin. Text after ';' is a comment.
tools.usage:
CHANGEREF <old> <new>
GATESWAP <ref1> <ref2>
PINSWAP <ref> <pin1> <pin2>
CHANGEPIN <ref> <pin1> <pin2>

parameters.name: pins
parameters.description: By number, or by name in double quotes, e.g. "D0".

tools.example:
CHANGEREF U1 U2 ; rename
GATESWAP U1A U1B ; swap gates
PINSWAP U5B "D0" "D1"
CHANGEPIN U3 5 6
tools.notes: List only the net change from the current state (U1 to U3, not U1 to U2 to U3). Back Annotate does not check part types before GATESWAP.

tools.name: .mnl (OrCAD Layout netlist)
tools.description: Netlist format for the legacy OrCAD Layout PCB tool, created from Tools > Create Netlist > Layout. DSN2MNL errors are written to an .ERR file. It is only needed for old Layout-based flows; OrCAD PCB Editor uses the pst*.dat netlist instead.
tools.usage: Tools > Create Netlist > Layout tab > <design>.MNL
tools.example: Regenerate amp.mnl to maintain a legacy board still in OrCAD Layout.

tools.name: .dbk / .obk (design and library backups)
tools.description: Automatic backups written on save: saving a project/design creates <design>.DBK and saving a library creates <library>.OBK, holding the previous version. Saving only a page or a part creates no backup.
tools.usage: Rename amp.DBK to amp_recovered.dsn and open it to recover the previous save.
tools.example: copy amp.DBK amp_prev.dsn
tools.notes: Rename a copy rather than the backup itself so the next save does not overwrite your recovery source.
